Source: A 32-year-old G1P0 woman at 12 weeks gestation presents to her obstetrician for a follow-up appointment.
At that time, she was found to have a thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) concentration <0.01 mU/L and an elevated free T4.
She reports mild improvement in her symptoms but continues to experience sweating and palpitations.
She was started on propranolol and propylthiouracil.
She has a past medical history of polycystic ovary syndrome.
She first presented 4 weeks ago with bilateral hand tremors.
Her family history is notable for hypothyroidism in her mother.
She does not smoke cigarettes, stopped drinking alcohol prior to pregnancy, and does not use drugs.
